transcript:
Header: 2026-03-17 11:00 PDT • Duration: 61 minutes • Attendees: Ari Turner, Leah Chen, Samir Patel, Maya Rodriguez, Jesse Park, Tanya Singh, plus all employees.

[00:00] Ari: hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy wednesday, welcome to the march all-hands. quick housekeeping, recording is on, the deck is in #all-hands, and we will go through leadership updates then q and a.

[00:15] Leah: quick note from infra — last week we had the mar 3 incident, brief recap, we hit a kernel scheduling bug in one of our quantized inference paths, that triggered a cascade on the dedicated pools causing higher latencies for about 40 minutes. we rolled back the kernel selection and routed traffic to the fallback variant, that bought us stability while we rolled a patch.

[00:35] Samir: yep, ops responded fast, shoutout to oncall. the important bit is we've added a safety circuit in the routing layer so if latency anomalies exceed threshold we automatically shift to compatible variants and notify the team. this cuts manual toil.

[00:50] Ari: thanks. Leah, what's next from a mitigation and long-term standpoint?

[01:00] Leah: we have three prongs: short-term patch to the kernel selector (deployed), medium-term is a more robust test harness to simulate kernel scheduler regressions in staging, and long-term is additional telemetry + automatic canarying for new kernel combos. goal is to avoid user-facing impact.

[01:20] Maya: on product, Dedicated adoption is up 26% q/q, we're seeing a lot of interest from mid-market and a few enterprise pilots asking for private deploy patterns. roadmap this quarter focuses on burst capacity controls, improved autoscaling policies, and an easier admin console for VPC onboarding.

[01:40] Ari: good. curious on any blockers from the sales side? Tanya?

[01:48] Tanya: sales reports security questions as the top blocker; customers want SOC2 evidence, encryption/KMS details, and for larger accounts, audit log retention and SSO. we're packaging a security packet to send and will run a webinar next month. also pricing questions on committed vs on-demand for Dedicated are recurring.

[02:10] Samir: engineering will prioritize the onboarding flow and add SAML SSO support for Dedicated 1.1. also working on improved tracing hooks so customers can get token-level latency breakdowns.

[02:30] Ari: ok, hiring — Jesse?

[02:35] Jesse: hiring momentum is steady; we closed 6 roles last month, ramping to 180 headcount by q2 target. interview loop adjustments: reduced take-home tests for staff+ engineers and added more product-led interviews. manager hires are slower; we need help from leaders to surface referrals.

[02:58] Ari: anything to call out on finances?

[03:02] Ari: high level — revenue and usage are in line with plan, gross margin improving due to some quantization and batching wins, but sales cycles for larger deals still lengthen due to security and procurement timelines. we are watching CAC and net retention closely.

[03:28] Leah: small note — we are also experimenting with a new kv cache tuning param that yields 7% cost reduction on conversational workloads in our benchmarks. still in A/B.

[03:45] Audience question (Employee): how are we measuring reliability SLOs across hosted vs dedicated?

[03:55] Samir: good q — hosted is measured by p95 latency and availability per region; for Dedicated we offer contractual SLAs on availability and per-model latency targets. console will expose per-route dashboards soon so teams can see token-level breakdowns.

[04:15] Audience (Employee): any change to open-source model catalog or supported quant formats?

[04:22] Maya: catalog remains curated, we'll add two new verified models next month and expand quantization profiles; customers can request additions via our model onboarding form.

[04:40] Audience: question about cost — how do batching and kv cache recommendations translate to customer bills?

[04:48] Leah: we have a redwood-optimize set of recommendations that estimate per-token $ impact; product will add a cost-savings simulator in the console.

[05:05] Ari: ok let's do a quick lightning updates — product, eng, people, customer success. Maya?

[05:12] Maya: quick — running a Dedicated pilot with FintechCo, initial benchmarks look promising (latency within target and 15% cost saving vs their in-house setup). will share the pilot brief after NDA.

[05:30] Samir: infra — working on autoscaling and a better canary deployment for kernel/quant changes. will have an internal alpha by end of month.

[05:45] Jesse: people — all hands reminder: manager check-ins, hiring referral bonuses increased for key roles, and mentoring program kicks off next week.

[06:00] Tanya: customer success — launched a new onboarding checklist for Dedicated; early feedback is that networking docs need to be clearer, we'll update that.

[06:15] Q&A continues, mix of live and chat questions. some transcribed highlights below.

[06:25] Employee (in chat): any timeline for private on-prem package?

[06:30] Maya: Private GA target is end of q3, with aviary on-prem alpha for select partners in q2. details to come in roadmap doc.

[06:42] Employee: will we open source any part of runtime?

[06:47] Leah: we will continue to contribute reference tooling and eval harnesses, but core runtime will remain productized for performance reasons. we'll publish more reproducible benchmarks.

[07:10] Wrap: Ari summarizes key takeaways: 1) incident learnings and routing safety circuit, 2) Dedicated momentum with security packaging as top sales ask, 3) hiring ramp and manager focus, 4) next steps and owners.

[07:30] Ari: thanks everyone, if you have follow-ups add them in #all-hands or ping me directly. recording and slides will be posted.

[07:40] End of recording.
